messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — canary v2.3.1 rolled at 1975302400 is showing a P95 regression specifically on short-sequence textgen workloads. Not a full outage but noticeable, ~6-9% on p95 across eu-west.

kevin: saw the alert. is this at 256 tokens or shorter? any deltas in batch sizes?

maya: mainly <64 tokens. throughput for long seq looks fine. I pulled a quick summary:

```
canary: v2.3.1
workload: short-seq (avg len 28)
baseline p95: 42ms
canary p95:   46ms
delta: +9.5% (eu-west)
cpu/gpu: nominal
mem spike: +120MB on host-12 during warmup
```

liam: interesting — mem bump during warmup could be KV cache path or new kernel selection. which kernel variant landed?

sara: v2.3.1 included the new aten-fused attention kernel (opt-3) that should help long seq, but we skipped the opt-2 fallback for short paths in this build.

kevin: ah that explains it. opt-3 reduces overhead for long sequences but has fixed per-call overhead that hurts tiny prompts. Can we route short requests to opt-2 for now?

maya: routing is configurable but the canary is a single binary variant in dedicated pool. We can do two options: 1) pause/stall the canary rollout and roll back to v2.3.0, or 2) patch runtime to add short-seq policy and redeploy a canary with mixed kernels.

liam: what's the risk window if we hold? SLA wise, this is below alerting for customers but we promised a p95 SLO for interactive apps. Ops doesn't recommend exposing rollback to customers during peak.

ops-bot: @channel Incident note: performance anomaly detected in canary pool eu-west. Current impact: increased p95 for short-seq generation. Affected quota: internal canary only.

kevin: can we try a temporary traffic-split to send 100% of short-seq traffic to stable v2.3.0 while keeping other traffic on canary? There is a routing rule API.

maya: I can add a query-length routing rule. Propose: if tokens_requested <= 64 -> stable, else -> canary. Would need a tiny config push. Risk: adds routing latency maybe +1ms.

sara: +1ms is acceptable compared to +4ms p95 regression. I'm in favor. If config push looks clean, do it.

kevin: agree. Maya, can you push the routing rule and monitor for 10m? If it looks stable we can continue the rollout. If not, rollback.

maya: pushing now. config snippet:

```json
{"routing_rules": [{"match": {"max_tokens": 64}, "route": "v2.3.0"}, {"default": "v2.3.1"}]}
```
deploy-bot: deploy started by maya at 1975302540. config-change-id: cfg-7783.

maya: done. rule applied to eu-west canary pool. watching metrics (p95, mem).

kevin: initial 2-min check?

maya: first 2 mins look good. p95 for short-seq back to 43ms. mem spike not reproducible now.

liam: nice. will start a targeted profiler run on opt-3 kernel to see why warmup had +120MB earlier. Can we get a heapdump window?

sara: schedule it during low traffic in 30m. Add sticky tags so profiler only samples canary nodes.

maya: noted. leaving routing rule in place for now. If profiler finds nothing, we'll try adding opt-2 fallback in the next canary build.

kevin: thanks. small follow-ups: 1) add a note in the release doc that opt-3 is not yet validated for short-seq; 2) mark this as 'hold-until-validated' for other regions.

maya: will update release notes and mute the p95 alert for canary pool to avoid noise (ops aware).

deploy-bot: deployment cfg-7783 succeeded at 1975302580.

ops-bot: monitoring baseline restored for short-seq path. No customer-facing impact observed.

maya: closing loop: routing kept users steady, profiler scheduled. If anyone wants to pair on the kernel profiling, ping me. :thumbsup:
